original_value: Calibration/Validation (Cal/Val) of satellite altimeters is fundamental for monitoring onboard sensor performance and ensuring long-term data quality. As altimeter technology has been evolving rapidly from profile to wide swath and interferometric altimetry, different requirements regarding Cal/Val have emerged. Most current Cal/Val technology has been developed for conventional profile altimeters, whereby satellite observations are compared against measurements at one point along orbit lines. However, the application of this type of Cal/Val technique to swath interferometric altimeters with two-dimensional measurements is difficult. Here, we propose a new strategy for the evaluation of interferometric altimeters based on comparison of wave-induced sea surface elevation (WSSE) spectra from one- and two-dimensional measurements. This method assumes that the WSSE variance of an equilibrium wave field is uniform and can be measured equivalently in the space or time domains. The method was first tested with simulated data and then used to evaluate the performance of an airborne interferometric radar altimeter system (AIRAS) using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) buoy measurements. The differences between the WSSE variances from the AIRAS and two GNSS buoys were below 8 cm2, corresponding to a standard deviation of 2.8 cm, which could serve as a reference for the WSSE error over the scale range of waves. The correlation coefficient between the AIRAS and GNSS buoys was approximately 0.90, indicating that the error was small relative to the WSSE signals. In addition, the sea surface height (SSH) difference measured by the AIRAS was compared with that derived from the GNSS buoys at two sites. The results indicated that the error of the SSH difference was 3 cm. This approach represents a possible technique for the Cal/Val of future spaceborne/airborne interferometric altimeters; however, additional experiments and applications are needed to verify the feasibility of this method.

result.paraphrase: Calibration/validation (Cal/Val) is essential to monitor onboard sensor performance and maintain long-term data quality for satellite altimeters. As altimetry has advanced quickly from profile to wide-swath and interferometric systems, the Cal/Val requirements have changed as well. Most existing Cal/Val methods were designed for conventional profile altimeters, comparing satellite observations with measurements at a single point along the orbit, but this approach is difficult to apply to swath interferometric altimeters that provide two-dimensional measurements. We therefore propose a new interferometric altimeter evaluation strategy based on comparing wave-induced sea surface elevation (WSSE) spectra from one-dimensional and two-dimensional measurements. The method assumes that WSSE variance in an equilibrium wave field is uniform and can be measured equivalently in either the space or time domain. It was first validated with simulated data and then applied to assess an airborne interferometric radar altimeter system (AIRAS) using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) buoy measurements. The WSSE variance differences between AIRAS and two GNSS buoys were under 8 cm2, corresponding to a standard deviation of 2.8 cm, which may serve as a reference for WSSE error across the wave scale range. The correlation coefficient between AIRAS and the GNSS buoys was about 0.90, suggesting that the error was small relative to the WSSE signals. In addition, sea surface height (SSH) differences measured by AIRAS were compared with those derived from the GNSS buoys at two sites. The results showed an SSH-difference error of 3 cm. This approach could be a promising Cal/Val technique for future spaceborne and airborne interferometric altimeters, though further experiments and applications are needed to confirm its feasibility.
